guide_enrichment.narrative:
For us, the case is less about reacting to Kansas’ opener and more about the ways this offense can create scoring opportunities. In his second career start, Isaiah Marshall completed 14 of 19 passes for 246 yards and two touchdowns while adding 49 rushing yards. Kansas finished with 613 total yards, and its offensive line allowed no sacks and only one tackle for loss. The opponent matters, so we are not treating that performance as proof, but it supports our view that Kansas can move the ball often enough to prevent the separation the market is pricing.

Our primary concern is Arizona State’s passing offense against a Kansas pass defense that grades poorly in the matchup data. Still, we think the market may be leaning too heavily into that weakness. Kansas returns cornerbacks Jalen Todd and Austin Alexander, who combined for 22 starts last season, along with safety Taylor Davis, who made 10 starts. That experience does not erase the efficiency concern, but it gives us enough reason to support our Kansas position rather than assume Arizona State consistently exploits the matchup.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We will be watching Arizona State’s passing game against the Kansas secondary. That is the matchup most capable of challenging our view, particularly if Arizona State repeatedly creates efficient scoring opportunities. Kansas did record 11 tackles for loss and three sacks in its opener, but we need to see whether that disruption carries over against a stronger opponent. If Kansas can keep the passing game from controlling the matchup, we think its own offense gives it a credible path to stay competitive throughout.

recent_game.fact: Kansas opened the 2026 season with a 51-6 home win over Long Island on Sept. 4.
Kansas produced 613 total yards on 76 plays against Long Island, including 277 rushing yards and 336 passing yards.
Kansas held Long Island to 146 total yards, 35 rushing yards on 33 attempts and no touchdowns.
Kansas recorded 11 tackles for loss and three sacks against Long Island.

opponent_notes.fact: Arizona State opened the 2026 season with a 70-7 win over Morgan State.
Arizona State is scheduled to play at Texas A&M on Sept. 12 before facing Kansas on Sept. 19.

quarterback.fact: Head coach Lance Leipold named redshirt sophomore Isaiah Marshall Kansas' starting quarterback before the 2026 season, replacing Jalon Daniels in the role.
In his second career start, Isaiah Marshall completed 14 of 19 passes for 246 yards and two touchdowns and rushed seven times for 49 yards against Long Island.
Backup Cole Ballard has played in 15 career games and entered the season with one career start.

Quarterback Chase Jenkins transferred to Kansas after starting all 12 regular-season games for Rice in 2025, when he passed for 1,025 yards and nine touchdowns and rushed for 531 yards and five touchdowns.

offensive_personnel.fact: Kansas returns two 2025 offensive-line starters: left tackle Calvin Clements and left guard Amir Herring, both of whom started all 12 games last season.
Kansas' offensive line allowed no sacks and only one tackle for loss against Long Island.
The Game 2 depth chart lists transfers Kasen Carpenter at center and Nick Morrow at right tackle, with Tavake Tuikolovatu at right guard.
Kansas added running backs Yasin Willis from Syracuse, Dylan Edwards from Kansas State and Jalen Dupree from Colorado State.
Against Long Island, Yasin Willis rushed 11 times for 72 yards and two touchdowns, Dylan Edwards had six carries for 32 yards and Jalen Dupree had nine carries for 35 yards and a touchdown.
Buffalo transfer Nik McMillan caught six passes for 130 yards and one touchdown in his Kansas debut, extending his streak to seven consecutive 100-yard receiving games.

defensive_personnel.fact: Defensive end Leroy Harris III recorded a career-high four tackles for loss against Long Island after leading Kansas with 4.5 sacks in 2025.
Michigan State transfer David Santiago recorded four tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery in his Kansas debut.
Linebacker Trey Lathan returns after leading Kansas with 86 tackles in 2025.
Kansas returns cornerbacks Jalen Todd and Austin Alexander, who combined for 22 starts in 2025, and safety Taylor Davis, who started 10 games in 2025.
Kansas added experienced safeties Corey Gordon and Jaden Harris; Gordon started all 12 games for Louisville in 2025, while Harris previously started 13 games for Miami in 2024.

coaching_changes.fact: Andy Kotelnicki returned to Kansas as associate head coach after two seasons at Penn State; he previously served as Kansas' offensive coordinator from 2021 through 2023.
D.K. McDonald is Kansas' defensive coordinator, and Daryl Agpalsa coaches the offensive line.

injury_availability.fact: Wide receiver Cam Pickett, who tied for Kansas' team lead with 45 receptions in 2025, did not play in the 2026 season opener; the notes do not state a reason.

offensive_context.fact: Kansas scored five rushing touchdowns against Long Island, with Willis scoring twice and Micah Johnson, Donald Collier and Jalen Dupree each scoring once.
Kansas generated six plays of more than 20 yards, including three plays of more than 40 yards, against Long Island.
Kansas has allowed 45 sacks since the start of the 2023 season, the second-fewest among Big 12 teams over that span.

defensive_context.fact: Kansas allowed 26.8 points and 387.2 total yards per game in 2025 under defensive coordinator D.K. McDonald.
Kansas allowed 214.1 passing yards per game in 2025, its lowest season average since 2001.
Kansas averaged 6.3 tackles for loss per game in 2025 and opened 2026 with 11 tackles for loss against Long Island.

special_teams.fact: Kansas added placekicker Martin Connington from Michigan State, punter Matthew Gill from Australia and long snapper Rino Monteforte from Cal for 2026.
Martin Connington made a 32-yard field goal and all six extra-point attempts against Long Island.
The Game 2 depth chart lists Tate Nagy as the primary punt returner and Dylan Edwards as the primary kickoff returner.

series_context.fact: Kansas and Arizona State have met once, with Arizona State winning 35-31 in Tempe on Oct. 5, 2024.

other_relevant.fact: Kansas and Arizona State are scheduled to play Sept. 19, 2026 at Wembley Stadium in London in each team's Big 12 opener.
The game will be Kansas' first international football game and the first Division I college football game played at Wembley Stadium.
